#### Full ORM, compile-time checked schema — the schema is generated Rust code, not runtime strings:

```rust
// schema.rs (auto-generated by `diesel print-schema`)
diesel::table! {
    users (id) {
        id -> Integer,
        name -> Text,
        email -> Text,
    }
}
```

```rust
use diesel::prelude::*;

#[derive(Queryable)]
struct User {
    id: i32,
    name: String,
    email: String,
}

let mut conn = SqliteConnection::establish("app.db").unwrap();

let results = users::table
    .filter(users::name.eq("Kurnia"))
    .load::<User>(&mut conn)
    .expect("query failed");

for u in results {
    println!("{}: {}", u.id, u.name);
}
```

#### Migrations live outside your code, run via `diesel_cli`:

```bash
diesel setup                       # creates DB + migrations dir
diesel migration generate create_users
diesel migration run               # applies pending migrations, regenerates schema.rs
```

⚠️ Heavy macro DSL (`table!`, `#[derive(Queryable)]`) — steepest learning curve of the three, and it's **synchronous only**, so it doesn't fit naturally into an async Axum/Tokio stack without wrapping every call in `spawn_blocking`.

✅ Payoff: queries are checked against `schema.rs` at compile time — rename a column, your build breaks instead of your prod query.
